newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Three more bodies pulled from Puerto Rico rubble.
newsitem.headline: Three more bodies pulled from Puerto Rico rubble.

text.p: Searchers on Sunday pulled three more bodies from the rubble of a San Juan commercial building devastated by a suspected gas explosion, authorities said.
The discoveries brought the number of victims found in the ruins to 25. Searchers suspect as many as 20 additional corpses may yet be found. At least 80 others were injured in the blast.

Crews resumed their search of the tangled wreckage on Saturday after being forced to wait more than 40 hours while sagging floors and walls were reinforced. Dogs trained to sniff out survivors found no signs of life when the search resumed.
The searchers included specially trained rescue teams from Miami and New York.

The six-story Humberto Vidal building, housing a shoe shop, jewelry store and offices above, was devastated on Thursday morning by an explosion that occurred just as the working day was beginning in Calle de Diego, a shopping street in San Juan's working class Rio Piedras district.
Federal investigators, including experts from the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, were at the scene to look for a cause.
During a visit to the site on Saturday, Gov. Pedro Rossello said the evidence pointed to a gas leak, but it would be a week or more before investigators could determine the cause.
